body:
Priya Shah: Seeing a spike in self-serve tickets: users running the RAG+agent quickstart are hitting 429s within a few minutes. Pattern: they run ingestion + a few chat requests, then get rate limited and assume the API is down. Anyone else seeing this?

Dev Patel: Yep. Support queue has 6 since yesterday. Most are free-trial / low-tier keys. They’re running the template as-is. One user pasted:
```
HTTP 429 Too Many Requests
{"error":{"type":"rate_limit","message":"Rate limit exceeded. Please retry later."}}
```
They’re asking what to set “qps” to.

Owen Phillips: Confirmed from escalation last night. Template is doing parallel retrieval eval + agent loop calls and we’re spiking concurrency. Even with retries, it’s basically hammering. Also: some users interpret 429 as “auth issue” because the template prints a generic error.

Monica Patel: That’s on us. Current defaults in the template are optimized for “feels fast” on our internal keys, not self-serve quotas. What’s the current concurrency setting in the released scaffold?

Dev Patel: From a ticket screenshot: they didn’t set anything; template started with “worker_count=8” (I think from uvicorn) and the client is doing up to 10 parallel calls when you hit `/ask` with streaming turned on.

Ibrahim Khan: For hosted API self-serve, 429 is expected when they exceed per-minute token/QPS. We should:
1) cap max in-flight requests in the template by default
2) implement exponential backoff with jitter AND respect `Retry-After` if present
3) error message should say “Rate limited (429). Reduce concurrency or request smaller outputs. See docs link.”

Brian Murphy: Gateway does return `Retry-After` for 429 in most cases. Some SDKs don’t surface it cleanly though. If the template is using raw fetch/requests, we can read the header and sleep. If it’s SDK, we need to confirm the error type exposes headers.

Henry Cho: +1. Also PM side: we should add guidance in docs and template README: “On free tier start with concurrency=1–2; don’t run eval harness + ingestion + chat at once.” We can make “eval” an explicit command that warns about quotas.

Renee Sullivan: From user interviews: people run `make dev` then immediately click around / spam refresh in the UI. They don’t know each refresh is a full generation. If the template includes a demo UI, we should debounce and maybe show “cooldown” when 429s happen.

Christine Wong: SRE angle: retries shouldn’t create a thundering herd. If we retry 429 aggressively we’ll keep them pinned at the limit and they’ll never recover. Backoff should be capped + jittered, and we should stop retrying after N attempts and surface actionable guidance.

Monica Patel: Agree. Concrete proposal for v1 patch:
- Default `MAX_CONCURRENT_LLM_REQUESTS=2` (and document it)
- Client retry policy:
  - retry on 429/503/504
  - base delay 0.5s, exponential *2, max 8s, jitter
  - if `Retry-After` present, prefer it (bounded)
  - max attempts 5
- If still failing: return a “Rate limited” message to user + log structured error with `error.category=quota`.

Dev Patel: Please also update troubleshooting playbook: “If you’re on free tier and seeing 429, lower concurrency and/or max_tokens.” We can paste a ready response for support.

Priya Shah: +1. What env var names do we want? We need something consistent across Python + TS templates.

Ibrahim Khan: Suggest `REDWOOD_MAX_INFLIGHT` (generic) and `REDWOOD_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS` / `REDWOOD_RETRY_MAX_DELAY_MS`. But keep it minimal for now: just `REDWOOD_MAX_INFLIGHT` and `REDWOOD_MAX_TOKENS`.

Brian Murphy: Please don’t call it QPS, since it’s more like concurrency + token budget. QPS is confusing when each request can be long streaming. “Max in-flight requests” is clearer.

Henry Cho: Also could add a note: “If you need higher throughput, upgrade tier or request limit increase.” But we should lead with “reduce concurrency” for self-serve.

Monica Patel: Action items:
- (Monica) PR to change template default concurrency + better error message for 429.
- (Ibrahim) verify SDK behavior re: `Retry-After` / headers. If missing, we’ll handle in template HTTP wrapper.
- (Priya/Dev) draft support macro + docs snippet for troubleshooting.
- (Renee) add UI debounce note if applicable.

Dev Patel: I’ll draft support macro today and share here for review.

Priya Shah: I’ll add this to top issues list for the troubleshooting page. Also, can we make the template print a one-time warning on startup like “Using default rate-limit safe settings (max in-flight=2). Set REDWOOD_MAX_INFLIGHT to tune.”?

Monica Patel: Yes. Also logging: when 429 happens, log `status=429`, `retry_after_s`, `inflight`, and the request id. (No prompt content.)

Brian Murphy: Request id should be in response header `x-redwood-request-id`. Capture it and print in error logs so support can trace.

Christine Wong: Can we ensure we don’t emit high-cardinality tags? Don’t tag metrics with request id. Log it, but metrics should aggregate.

Priya Shah: Good call. We’ll keep request id only in logs.

Dev Patel: Draft macro v0:
“429 means your key hit rate limits. Reduce concurrent requests (set REDWOOD_MAX_INFLIGHT=1 or 2), reduce max_tokens, and avoid running eval + ingestion + chat simultaneously. If the issue persists after a few minutes, share x-redwood-request-id from logs and we can investigate.”

Monica Patel: Looks good. I’ll post PR link when up.

Henry Cho: Once merged, let’s also note in release notes: “Adjusted defaults to be friendly for self-serve quotas.”

Priya Shah: Thanks all. Marking this thread as the tracking place for the 429 default issue until PR is merged.
